Use a relevant chemical equation to calculate the pH of a 0.20 mol L⁻¹ solution of N₂H₅⁺ using the following data:

questions.stimulus: Hydrazine is a compound of hydrogen and nitrogen. The complete combustion of 1.0 L of gaseous hydrazine requires 3.0 L of oxygen, producing 2.0 L of nitrogen dioxide gas and 2.0 L of water vapour. All volumes are measured at 400°C. The relationship between the acid equilibrium constant (Ka) and the corresponding conjugate base equilibrium constant (Kb) is shown. Ka × Kb = Kw

criteria.text: Correctly calculates the pH ; Provides a correct chemical equation
Provides the main steps of the calculation
Provides some steps of the calculation OR Provides a correct chemical equation
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer:
Hydrazinium ion, N₂H₅⁺, reacts with water to produce an acidic solution in the following way:
N₂H₅⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + N₂H₄(aq)
[ICE table: R row N₂H₅⁺(aq) 0.20, H₂O(l) –, H₃O⁺(aq) 0, N₂H₄(aq) 0; C row −x, –, +x, +x; E row (0.20 − x), –, x, x]
Ka = Kw / Kb = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 1.7 × 10⁻⁶ = 5.88 × 10⁻⁹
Assume equilibrium concentration of N₂H₅⁺ = 0.20 mol L⁻¹ (ie, x is very small)
Ka = [H₃O⁺][N₂H₄] / [N₂H₅⁺] = 5.88 × 10⁻⁹
x² / 0.20 = 5.88 × 10⁻⁹
x = √(5.88 × 10⁻⁹ × 0.20)
x = 3.43 × 10⁻⁵ = [H₃O⁺]
pH = −log₁₀(3.43 × 10⁻⁵) = 4.46

questions.stem: How do collision theory and Le Chatelier’s principle account for the colour change to pink when the solution is cooled? Refer to the energy profile diagram in your answer.
questions.stimulus:
A purple solution at 25°C contains a mixture of two different cobalt(II) complexes which are at equilibrium. CoCl₄²⁻(aq) + 6H₂O(l) ⇌ Co(H₂O)₆²⁺(aq) + 4Cl⁻(aq) (blue) (pink) The results of heating and cooling a sample of this solution are given in the table. Temperature (°C) | 80 | 0
Colour of solution | blue | pink
The energy profile diagram for this reaction is shown. [Energy profile diagram: vertical axis labelled Enthalpy, horizontal axis labelled Reaction coordinate. The Reactants level is higher than the Products level. Ea1 is marked from the Reactants level up to the peak of the curve; Ea2 is marked from the peak down to the Products level.]

criteria.text: Shows how both Le Chatelier’s principle AND collision theory account for the colour change, with reference to the energy profile
Demonstrates a sound understanding of how both collision theory AND Le Chatelier’s principle account for the colour change
Demonstrates a sound understanding of how collision theory OR Le Chatelier’s principle accounts for the colour change
Demonstrates some understanding of collision theory OR Le Chatelier’s principle
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: The energy profile diagram shows that the forward reaction is exothermic. Le Chatelier’s principle considers heat as a ‘substance’ that the system seeks to replace when lost. As this system is cooled, it responds in a way as to minimise the disturbance. Consequently, the forward reaction is favoured so the solution turns pink. Collision theory considers the proportion of molecules above a particular activation energy. Decreasing the temperature slows the rates of both forward and reverse reactions, due to a drop in the average kinetic energy of all particles. However, the rate of the reverse reaction decreases more than the forward reaction. This is due to a greater proportion of particles falling below the relatively higher activation energy of the reverse reaction, Ea2, as shown in the reaction profile. Since the forward reaction is faster, [CoCl₄²⁻] will decrease, and [Co(H₂O)₆²⁺] will increase, and the colour changes to pink.
